title: Budget-aware QuickCards: scope reduction for Console micro-tiles (dashboards, trace sampling, cost deltas)
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Propose an MVP cut that delivers a compact, budget-focused dashboard card set called 'Budget-aware QuickCards'. Each QuickCard presents route-level cost delta, percentage change vs baseline, and a single-line tracer sample link (opens sampled traces). The full tracing explorer and per-token breakdown are out-of-scope for MVP and will be delivered later under Console Insights Phase 2.

Problem statement: Customers need a lightweight way to see cost regressions and the most likely route causing them without paying the telemetry and UI cost of full trace graphs in the initial launch. The current Console scope includes heavy trace visualizations and granular per-request token cost; those are driving delivery complexity and cost.

MVP cut proposal:
- Deliver 3 QuickCard types: Route delta card, Top-3 spenders card (aggregated), and Budget status card (green/amber/red).
- Replace the heavy trace explorer with a 1-click "Open sampled trace" link on each route card that opens an external trace viewer (instrumented by Eng in runtime) or navigates to the lightweight sampling detail panel. No timeline waterfall or span explorer in MVP.
- Cost breakdown limited to top-3 contributors per route (service/model combo). No token-by-token cost, no model-level kernel profiling.
- Feature gated: QuickCards are behind a console feature flag and default to disabled for existing customers until rollout.

Why this cut: Significant reduction in telemetry ingestion, UX surface, and implementation complexity while preserving the core value: fast detection of cost regressions with actionable next steps.
acceptance_criteria: QuickCards render on the Console route overview page and respect user/project-level budget configs.
Each Route delta QuickCard shows: route name, cost delta (7d vs 28d baseline), percentage change, and color-coded indicator (green/amber/red) based on thresholds configured via Console settings.
Top-3 spenders QuickCard lists up to 3 service/model pairs with aggregated spend percentage and absolute USD delta; clicking a spender drills to a filtered Logs/Usage page.
Sampled trace link present on each QuickCard that opens sampled trace in the lightweight panel or redirects to the external trace viewer; link logs telemetry for click-through metrics.
Feature flag toggles QuickCards; when disabled, Console shows a compact fallback message linking to full Cost Explorer.
API/Backend: endpoints return summarized cost delta and top contributors within 2s P95 for typical project sizes (baseline defined in ENG- baseline performance doc).
E2E tests that simulate a synthetic cost spike resulting in QuickCard color transition from green -> red within the card refresh window (test runs in CI).
Docs: PRD and user-facing help article published prior to release, and a migration note for customers reliant on the old heavy trace cards.
decisions: Cut full trace explorer and span waterfall from MVP in favor of a sampled-trace link (reduces UI scope and trace ingestion).
Limit cost breakdown to top-3 contributors to keep payloads small and iterate on finer granularity later.
Expose color thresholds as settings rather than hard-coding so early enterprise customers can tune alarms without product changes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind account opt-in; internal beta for 3 pilot customers and Redwood dev org (2 weeks).
Phase 1: Gradual rollout to 10% of new Console users, monitor error rates, click-through, and cost of telemetry (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Expand to 100% with doc emails and in-product highlights if no regressions in key metrics (2 weeks).
Rollback: Toggle feature flag off and show fallback card if API errors > 0.5% or backend latency P95 > 3s for 10m window.
qa_checks: Smoke: QuickCards render for projects with and without budgets configured.
Load: Backend summarization endpoint holds P95 < 2s for synthetic dataset of 50k routes.
Security: Trace sampling link respects RBAC and does not expose sample IDs to unauthorized users.
Metrics: Instrument click-through, card renders, and color transitions; alert if CTR < 1% after pilot (indicates UX or data issues).
